name: preview_revert
description: What reverting one of your changes, one of your runs, or your own changes in one task you ran in would do, without doing it: each row the revert would restore (RESTORE) and each row it would leave alone because someone changed it after the agent (SKIP, with the reason). People win: a skipped row is never overwritten. The preview runs the revert on trial and rolls it back. Nothing is reverted here: only a person can revert, with their passkey. To hand them the revert, call request_revert with the same scope (it returns a link to show them). Another agent's change or run, or a task you never ran in, is NOT_FOUND, the same as an unknown id; in a task, the person can include other agents' changes on the signing page. Name exactly one of changeId, runId, taskId. Lines are cursor-paginated in their signed order. Any size can be previewed; a revert over 1000 lines becomes a plan the agent applies in batches after the person signs it (revert_plan, apply_revert_batch). The result carries nextSteps when there is something to do: do them in order.

changeId.description: Revert one change (a revert's own changeId reverts that revert).

runId.description: Revert every applied change of one run.

taskId.description: Revert your own applied changes in one task you ran in (you have a run with that task id); only your own lines. The person can include other agents' changes on the signing page. A task you never ran in is NOT_FOUND.

runs.description: Only with taskId, 1 to 20 of your own runs with that task id; the preview holds only their lines. Absent: all your runs in the task.

resources.description: 1 to 20 resource names, each one you wrote in this scope (Postgres: schema.table names); the preview holds only their lines. Absent: every resource.

select.description: Planned (revert scope, RS-3): the scope descriptor the preview covers, as the store normalized it: agents is exactly [agent:<your name>]; its runs and resources keys hold your runs and resources filters, or null.

rows.description: RESTORE lines in the whole preview.

skipped.description: SKIP lines in the whole preview.

op.description: The inverse write the revert would run.

now.description: The row as it is now. Absent when redacted.

set.description: The values the revert would write. Absent when redacted.

redacted.description: True when this agent cannot read the row (in Postgres, cannot SELECT its table); key and values are hidden.

largeValues.description: CONTRACT.md, Large values: the values (key, now, set) of this line left out because they are too large for you to read, each with its size and sha256; absent when none was. A value left out is absent from its object, never null: it is stored in full and a revert restores it from the stored row. An image with largeValues is not the whole row: never rebuild a row or a write from it.

moreChangeIds.description: CONTRACT.md, Large values: changeIds holds at most the first 100 changes that touched this row; this counts the rest. Absent when none was left out.

nextSteps.description: Planned (CONTRACT.md, Next steps): what to do next, first step first.

personMessage.description: Planned (CONTRACT.md, Next steps): the message the agent shows the person verbatim, keeping its line breaks; each URL on a line of its own (planned, M3.5) (CONTRACT.md, Showing links).

links.description: The URLs of personMessage with labels, in order; present exactly when personMessage holds a URL.
